Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles 289 through 371 of the Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, January 27, 1962, as amended); Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, September 27, 2001, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 24415, December 30, 2012, as amended); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Anonymity (Act No. 5493, January 5, 1997, as amended); Financial Services Commission regulations implementing FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 on beneficial ownership transparency and the identification of customers and beneficial owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry of the competent Korean District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document is issued by a Korean authority and will be used in a Hague Apostille Convention state, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea must append an apostille to the court-issued certificate; consular legalization is not required. If the destination state is not a party to the Apostille Convention, the certificate must instead be channeled exclusively through consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two methods are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Existing Corporate Registration Record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry of the competent Korean District Court and the National Tax Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The registry extract is authenticated by apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for use in an Apostille Convention state. For a non-Apostille state, the extract is submitted to the Korean consular post having jurisdiction for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel routes and must not be applied in combination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed or interim entity, with signature acknowledgement by a licensed Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution and power of attorney are first notarized by a Korean notary under the Korean Authentication Act. For an Apostille Convention destination, the notarized instrument is then submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea for an apostille. For a non-Apostille destination, the notarized instrument is submitted to the Korean Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization. Only one path is used depending on the destination state; sequential combination of both is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporating shareholders and authenticated copy filed with the Commercial Registry of the competent Korean District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The authenticated registry copy must be apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea if the destination state is an Apostille Convention state. If the destination state is not an Apostille Convention state, the authenticated copy must be consular legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The apostille and consular legalization channels are exclusive alternatives and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and AML/KYC Due Diligence Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean commercial bank holding the proposed corporation's preliminary account or an international bank providing the initial finance reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature is notarized by a Korean notary, after which the document is apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea for use in an Apostille Convention state. For a non-Apostille state, the notarized bank letter is consular legalized at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The alternative paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each legal person, ultimate beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory must be screened before incorporation and at all onboarding touchpoints against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and UN sanctions designations, (ii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, (iii) the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, (iv) the Korean FIU designation and warning notices, and (v) a proprietary PEP database covering senior foreign political officials, their immediate family members, and close associates. Any positive match must trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and suspicion report filing to the Korean FIU under Articles 4 through 6 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. Negative news and adverse-media checks are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS) at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, a company trade name must be stated in the Korean alphabet (Hangul) and must identify the corporate form as Chusik Hoesa. A Latin-script transliteration may be used as a supplementary foreign trade name, but the operative domestic legal name on the registry, tax certificate, and official invoices must be Hangul. The four-tier naming review requires: (1) a distinctive core trade-name component; (2) an objectively stated business-purpose clause; (3) the mandatory entity suffix Chusik Hoesa; and (4) confirmation of no identity or near-identity with an existing Korean company engaged in the same or similar business. The iROS search must be repeated immediately before the registration filing because the system does not grant a formal indefinite freeze to an unregistered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Registry rejects a proposed name, the incorporating party may, within two weeks from receipt of the rejection notice, file a written appeal with the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal must state the rejected trade name, the iROS search certificate number, the statutory basis for distinctiveness, and detailed arguments against any finding of public confusion or identity with an existing company. If the district court upholds the rejection, an immediate appeal to the High Court is available. In parallel, the applicant may submit a modified name through iROS and should not reuse the rejected name while the appeal is pending. The incorporation registration may only proceed once the new name is accepted or a final court decision reverses the registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act, the company must designate a physical head-office address in Korea in its articles and register that address with the district court. For an ISIC 6201 B2B enterprise SaaS company, a shared workspace or commercial receptionist address may initially satisfy the registry if it is a real street address in Korea. However, the National Tax Service may require evidence of actual office control before issuing the business registration certificate, and Korean banks under AML and branch operational guidance generally conduct an on-site visit or demand a lease, utility bill, and confirmation that responsible personnel can receive official mail. A pure virtual office, a commercial mailbox, or a P.O. Box is not acceptable for a corporate bank account or for VAT invoice registration in this industry. A home-office registration is permissible only if the resident director or employee actually works at that address and the address is disclosed consistently to the registry, tax office, and bank. For a cross-border funded SaaS entity, substance is strengthened by a dedicated lease, a physical company sign, and at least one locally available compliance or administrative officer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspections are possible by municipal tax officers and registry officials under the Framework Act on Local Taxes and the Commercial Act. For a low-risk B2B SaaS company, the quantified risk is approximately 25 to 35 percent within the first 18 months when the registered office is a virtual suite with no resident director; below 10 percent when the company maintains a dedicated lease, a visible sign, and a resident director; and minimal at approximately 5 percent when a full dedicated office with staff is maintained. Inspection checklist: (1) lease agreement or title deed; (2) company name plate on the door; (3) functioning workstations and office equipment; (4) a resident director or employee on site; (5) cloud infrastructure or server documentation; (6) tax invoices and accounting records; (7) official mail delivery; (8) independent telephone or data lines; (9) board minutes and compliance files; and (10) bank statements matching the declared address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance search through iROS online portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for online name search and preliminary availability in Korea.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Notary Fee Schedule based on stated authorized capital; prevailing market range 150 to 500 USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration tax on stated capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration tax at the statutory rate of 0.4 percent of stated capital, plus a 20 percent local education tax surcharge, approximated at 0.48 percent of capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: District court commercial registration filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry of the competent District Court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory court fees under the Rules on Litigation Fees as indexed to the registration case type and stated capital ceiling.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate issuance and VAT registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government fee for issuance of the business registration certificate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registry extracts and certificates of incorporation and good standing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry of the competent District Court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry extract certificate fee per certified copy, approximately 30 USD total for the bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille fees for five documentary instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee per apostille, approximately 6 to 12 USD per document; no consular legalization fee where the Apostille Convention applies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal retainer for Stage 1 cross-border due diligence and incorporation compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean law firm or professional corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Korean Bar Association and international corporate practice benchmark for cross-border Chusik Hoesa formation, fixed fee plus disbursements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML, UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening database checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance screening platform or licensed corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-scope enhanced due diligence fee, typically 200 to 400 USD for the complete shareholder and management chain.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First year registered office and virtual office or shared workspace service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial office landlord or licensed co-working space provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental benchmark in Seoul central business district for a small software-natured commercial address, mail handling, and basic reception service.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended, including Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 313, 316 and 317 on incorporation and registration, Article 330 on par value, and Articles 383 et seq. on board governance); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) Articles 5 and 6; Court Fees and Registration Tax laws; and the Act on the Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization for digital service activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Civil Registry Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; for a Seoul principal office, the Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court; post-registration business and tax registration with the competent District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; foreign investment reporting with Invest Korea (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, filed together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), subscription statements, certificate of paid-in capital deposit, consent-to-appointment forms of directors and statutory auditor, and the corporate seal registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a Korean Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The subscribed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully deposited into a dedicated Korean bank account in the name of the promoter or pre-incorporation entity before the court registration is submitted. No blocked escrow account is required for a general B2B enterprise SaaS business. If the foreign investor remits aggregate investment equal to or greater than KRW 100,000,000, or will hold at least 10% of voting shares, a foreign investment report must be accepted by Invest Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank before incorporation; the capital remittance must be sourced and documented through normal banking channels.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole incorporator of the Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) and by its first board of directors, that: WHEREAS, the incorporator has subscribed for 1,000,000 common shares, each with a par value of KRW 100, at an aggregate subscription price of KRW 100,000,000; and WHEREAS, the full subscription price has been paid and deposited into a dedicated corporate capital-subscription bank account in the Republic of Korea in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act; and WHEREAS, the approved Articles of Incorporation state that the company’s business purpose is the development, licensing, deployment, maintenance, and support of enterprise cloud software and B2B SaaS services, together with related data processing, cloud infrastructure services, and information technology consulting; and WHEREAS, the incorporation registration will be filed with the competent District Court under Article 317 of the Commercial Act; NOW BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The subscription and issuance of 1,000,000 common shares at a par value of KRW 100 per share, at par, are ratified and confirmed, and the aggregate paid-in capital of the company is fixed at KRW 100,000,000. 2. The registered office of the company is hereby adopted as the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and all statutory notices, legal process, and corporate records shall be maintained at that address. 3. The directors named in the Articles of Incorporation are confirmed as the first board of directors, and the board hereby appoints the designated Representative Director as Chief Executive Officer, the designated officer as Chief Financial Officer, and, where applicable under the Commercial Act, the statutory auditor, each to serve until the first annual general meeting of shareholders. 4. The Representative Director is authorized, individually, to open, maintain, and close bank accounts; to sign or endorse checks, promissory notes, mandates, and payment instructions; and to act as the sole or joint authorized signatory for banking and treasury operations. 5. The Representative Director and Corporate Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute, deliver, and file all documents required for the company’s incorporation registration, business registration with the National Tax Service, foreign investment report, e-tax registration, social insurance registrations, and any other regulatory filings. 6. The board directs that the corporate seal, specimen seal certificate, shareholder register, share certificates, board meeting minutes, and accounting books be prepared, authenticated, and kept at the registered office. 7. The board waives formal notice of this first board meeting, confirms that this resolution was adopted by unanimous consent, and directs the Corporate Secretary to certify and distribute copies of this resolution as needed for banking, registration, and counterparty due diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Subscription Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Invest Korea (KOTRA) One-Stop Foreign Investment Service, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, or a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea; the depository bank’s corporate banking department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor, or an agent with a notarized power of attorney, must file the foreign investment report with Invest Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank if the aggregate investment reaches KRW 100,000,000 or the investor will hold at least 10% of voting shares. The report must identify the investor, proposed Korean company name, ISIC 6201 B2B enterprise SaaS business description, capital subscription plan, and remittance route. After the report is accepted, open a temporary capital-deposit bank account in the name of the promoter or the pre-incorporation entity at a licensed Korean bank, remit the full paid-in capital, obtain wire-transfer records and a certificate of deposit or verified bank passbook, and execute the source-of-funds declarations required under AML/KYC rules. This step ends only when the full subscription capital is verified and the foreign investment report certificate, if applicable, is issued.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate certificate of the foreign investor
Power of attorney, notarized and apostilled or consular legalized as applicable
Company name reservation receipt or intended corporate name and business purpose description
Paid-in capital remittance instructions and bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is queried, correct the ownership, business description, or capital amount and resubmit through the same portal within five business days. If the bank suspends the capital deposit because of AML/KYC concerns, provide a detailed source-of-wealth statement, bank statements for remitting accounts, and any organizational ownership chart; request the bank’s compliance team to escalate the review in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean notary public authorized under the Korean Notary Act; the notary’s office in the jurisdiction where the incorporators execute the document.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean commercial form, setting out the corporate name, capital amount, number and par value of shares, business purpose for enterprise cloud software and B2B SaaS, registered office address, composition of the first board of directors, statutory auditor, accounting period, and calling method for meetings. The incorporators or their appointed attorneys must execute the Articles in person before the notary public. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, confirms the subscription terms, checks the name and business-purpose clauses against mandatory Commercial Act requirements, and issues a notarial certificate for the Articles. Any correction after notarization requires a supplementary notarial act; therefore the draft should be pre-reviewed by Korean counsel. The Articles must be consistent with the capital deposit amount verified in Step 1.
required_dossiers: English and Korean drafts of Articles of Incorporation
Valid passport or ID of each incorporator and director
Power of attorney for any proxy incorporator
Proof of Korean address or registered office location
Bank certificate of subscription capital deposit
Written approval of Articles from all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to notarize because of an inconsistency, prepare a corrective supplement, obtain signature of all incorporators, and return to the notary. If a director or incorporator is absent, obtain an additional notarized power of attorney; if the business-purpose clause is considered too broad, amend to limit it to enterprise software, SaaS, and related IT consulting before re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation and Post-Incorporation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate banking department of the chosen licensed Korean commercial bank; Registrar or Corporate Secretary function established by the board.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business registration certificate is issued, activate or convert the temporary capital-deposit account into a permanent corporate operating bank account. Provide the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, notarized Articles, representative director ID, seal impression certificate, and a certified copy of the first board resolution authorizing banking representatives. The bank will complete KYC/AML screening, issue account signatory mandates, and may require the beneficial-owner declaration. Following account opening, the company should issue share certificates, execute a shareholders’ register, maintain the registered office corporate seal, and hold the next board meeting to validate all pre-incorporation contracts. The Representative Director should verify that the statutory annual meeting schedule and accounting records comply with the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate and business registration certificate
Certified copy of the first board resolution
Power of attorney for external service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial-ownership documentation, provide an ownership chart, passport copies, and the foreign investment report certificate. If the bank declines to open an account for the initial capital amount, increase the capital or provide a written business plan and revenue forecast. If the bank requires a residence registration proof for the officer, use the corporate registered-office consent letter and legal counsel attestation to satisfy the compliance team.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 enterprise cloud software development and B2B SaaS is a digital services activity; no Korean industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing license is triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or physical production operating permit applies to this entity’s stated scope of business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Korean Ministry of Environment EIA procedures under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act are not triggered for pure software and SaaS operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - no Full EIA, partial EIA, or Environmental Registration is required because the company will not operate industrial facilities, factories, or chemical plants.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no point-source wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, stack emissions, hazardous waste, or chemical handling thresholds; general office waste electrical and electronic equipment must still be handled under the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit or separate industrial fire safety certification is required for a digital enterprise SaaS company. The company, as a tenant of an ordinary office, must only ensure that the leased premises possess valid fire safety and building-use approvals in accordance with the Fire Protection and Occupational Safety and Health standards of local government; this is a landlord/building obligation, not a company operating-license requirement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic tax portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity commencing taxable activity in South Korea, the entity must appoint a domestic tax representative if it does not have a place of business in Korea. The representative then files a business registration application with the competent District Tax Office (or the Seoul Regional Tax Office for cross-jurisdictional cases) using the HomeTax e-filing system. The issued Business Registration Number (BRN) is a 10-digit number serving as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration ID. Required documentation includes the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, evidence of foreign registration, board resolution authorizing the Korean registration, power of attorney in favor of the tax representative, and the completed statutory application for business registration. Registration must be completed before commencing taxable supplies in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa corporate entity. The entity is taxed separately on its worldwide income under the Korean Corporate Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch elective regimes are available to a domestic corporation; controlled foreign company (CFC) rules and other anti-avoidance provisions apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold; any person engaging in a taxable business must register with the National Tax Service before commencement of business. For natural persons (individuals only), a simplified VAT taxpayer ceiling of KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover may apply, but a Chusik Hoesa corporation is not eligible for simplified taxpayer status and must obtain full VAT registration from the start of business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issuance is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Each e-tax invoice must be transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax system by no later than the day following issuance. There is no pre-clearance or real-time fiscal stamping requirement at issuance; however, the NTS operates an anti-fraud central validation and matching system that cross-checks e-tax invoice data, cash receipt statements, credit card transaction summaries, and tax returns. Non-compliance, late transmission, or failure to issue valid e-tax invoices triggers additional VAT penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are physically exported from South Korea under applicable customs law. Export-related services, including B2B enterprise SaaS and digital services supplied to non-resident customers, are zero-rated where the place of supply is determined to be outside South Korea, the service is not physically consumed in Korea, and the consideration is received in foreign currency. The supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence demonstrating non-resident status of the recipient, the offshore nature of the service, and the receipt of foreign currency payment on a repatriated basis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration submitted via UNI-PASS)
Commercial invoice and detailed service contract
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Currency Exchange Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank
Proof of service delivery or usage metrics confirming the foreign recipient's actual receipt of the digital service
Certificate or written confirmation from the foreign customer evidencing non-resident business establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the zero-rating claim lacks sufficient statutory documentation, the NTS will deny the 0% rate and reclassify the supply as taxable, assessing 10% VAT retroactively. Underdeclared VAT arising from unjustified zero-rating is subject to statutory interest and additional tax penalties; intentional false claims, fraudulent export invoices, or fictitious customs declarations may lead to criminal prosecution, monetary fines, and confiscation orders. The NTS also retains a five-year statutory assessment period for VAT, enabling retrospective clawback of improper zero-rating benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) in statutory coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), the Korea Customs Service, and the Foreign Exchange Information Network; MOEF is the primary regulator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, while BOK operates settlements and reserve policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won operates under a free-floating exchange-rate regime with separate current and capital account disciplines. Current-account foreign exchange payments, including SaaS subscription royalties, software licence fees, dividends and service remuneration, are freely convertible as long as the remitting corporate client lodges an accurate foreign-exchange purpose code and supporting transaction history with an authorised foreign exchange bank. Korean banks do not impose a surrender tax or convertibility spread for commercial trade; however, the bank must conduct an economic-substance review before every non-trade dividend or profit remittance. Capital-account flows are not fully liberalised: equity injections, external loans, and derivative transactions require declaration, notification, approval, or post-reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Profit remittance from a Chusik Hoesa is operationally possible after the company submits its audited or reviewed financial statements, tax clearance documents, board resolution, and proof that underlying export proceeds have been collected through a resident foreign-exchange bank within the statutory period. A common delayed-exit hurdle is the 'business legitimacy test' applied to foreign UBOs in non-Korean holding structures; the bank will need the offshore chain to be fully visible, with share certificates, source-of-wealth evidence, and prior-year tax filings. The current account is therefore convertible, while capital account convertibility is conditional, monitored, and substantially easier for real FDI than for portfolio instruments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from provided software and services must be physically credited to a resident 'foreign exchange bank' in Korea within 180 calendar days from the date of export/customs declaration or the service completion certificate. This statutory collection period may be extended by an additional 180 days with a documented reason submitted to MOEF/BOK before maturity. There is no blanket percentage-forced conversion quota under the current Korean market-rate system; exporters may retain foreign currency in an onshore foreign currency account, but any conversion to KRW must be settled through the bank at the prevailing market rate and the trade must be continuously reportable to the BOK exchange information system. The 'surrender' requirement is therefore a financial reporting and repatriation requirement rather than a xenocurrency expropriation rule, and every foreign-exchange purchase or sale must be backed by a designated purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Proceeds) and Basic Operating KRW Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with integrated export collection and foreign currency sweep
Trade Settlement and SaaS Billing Collection Account (FCY/KRW dual ledger)
SWIFT-clearing and Documentary Collection Settlement Account for outbound licensing payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a legal settlement rail for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Foreign EMIs (Stripe Billing, Wise B2B) are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Korea and cannot legally provide KRW-denominated account numbers, custody, or foreign-exchange clearing services that satisfy the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They may be used as payment-gateway front-ends or as collection agents that compress transaction data, provided every actual fiat settlement is swept onward to a resident Tier-1 bank. The bank's compliance committee should treat EMI statements as secondary evidence and require final MT103/MT202 confirmations on a licensed Korean bank branch. For regulated capital injections or export-proceeds surrender, the EMI structure is not acceptable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory director or the registered resident manager of the Korean Chusik Hoesa must attend a physical onboarding interview at a domestic branch of the Tier-1 bank. Remote consular proxy account opening is not generally permitted for a newly incorporated enterprise with non-resident controlling shareholders. Foreign statutory directors holding only a consular certificate will be required to supply a Korean Alien Registration Card (or the equivalent resident ID), whereas a Korean-resident director may sign the account-opening questionnaire. If no local director exists, the bank will require a notarised power of attorney granting transaction-signing authority to a resident employee/agent, plus an in-person verification of that agent's identity; the foreign director must still be screened through an additional FCU interview, usually via documented video call with two-person independent verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the beneficial owner is a natural person resident outside South Korea holding the Chusik Hoesa through an intermediate holding company in a tax-haven or low-disclosure jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry excerpts for each entity in the ownership chain, notarised shareholders' register from the last annual filing, BOK-compatible UBO declaration form, source-of-wealth package (bank reference, tax assessment, audited financials), and an organisational chart signed by that UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual receivables pattern: the enterprise software exporter receives multiple small-amount subscription payments from countries outside Korea and the bank sees no conventional trade contract or enterprise customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed B2B SaaS agreements with enterprise counterparties, full invoice and subscription ledger extracted from Stripe including payment settlement details, IP licensing certificate and technology service contract, end-customer KYC summary, and a written explanation of the chosen commitment-to-settlement routing path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency: the company's registered address is only an tax-agent or law-firm address and there are no payroll lines, utility bills, or physical operation records in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office lease agreement in the entity's name, employment contracts and four-quarter payroll statements (or a resident employer records), fixed-line telecom bills, business-insurance policy in the company's name, and dated photographs/board minutes showing management activity at the Korean office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty red flags: the bank identifies sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions among the SaaS licensee population and cannot confirm why the Korean entity receives funds from customers in unlisted FX-control states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party sanctions screening report covering licensees, commercial invoices and counterparty declarations of final use, legal opinion confirming the software is an ordinary commercial product not subject to export-control licensing, and an internal policy requiring each foreign customer to pass minimum AML due diligence before activation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial equity capital of the Chusik Hoesa, the foreign investor must remit the Korean won equivalent in foreign currency from an overseas bank via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to a 'Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account' opened at an approved Tier-1 Korean bank branch under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The bank will assign the correct foreign-exchange purpose code (Foreign Direct Investment/Equity); it must secure a 'Declaration of Foreign Investment' before the remittance or use the post-declaration route if no advance report is required for the announced amount. After the funds are received, the bank registers the investment and issues a certificate of foreign-investment reporting; the company then issues shares, deposits the subscribed amount into the operating account, and obtains a capital verification certificate from the foreign-exchange bank and a notarised corporate stamp. The same regulated path will apply for further paid-in capital increases and must not be substituted by EMI fronting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 low-value/high-volume SaaS subscription settlement for export invoices; (2) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for treasury transfers between the company's foreign-currency account and any international assembly; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC at sight or usance) where contractual obligations require documentary protection; and (4) Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for long-term enterprise licensing arrangements. Software exports do not have customs declarations, so the bank will accept the signed service contract, delivery/access logs, and invoice ledger as the export evidence. All outbound disbursement rails must include the applicable foreign-exchange purpose code and must not escape the six-month repatriation rule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD and KRW/EUR forward contracts covering documented export receivables or import/expense payables with a maturity aligned to the underlying invoice or royalty collection date.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) with a licensed counterparty for hedging long-term foreign-investment loans, intercompany debt, or subscribed-capital repatriation commitments under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available only through an authorised foreign bank branch for non-resident hedging moments where onshore physical KRW settlement cannot be delivered; domestic Chusik Hoesa treasury desk is normally restricted to onshore deliverable instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regular General Shareholders' Meeting and approval of audited financial statements and disposal of accumulated earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa convened at the company's head office; no government filing body is involved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the close of each business year; for a calendar-year company whose fiscal year ends December 31, the meeting must be held no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee applies, but failure to hold the meeting and approve the financial statements prevents directors from obtaining a valid discharge from liability; violations of the Korean Commercial Act meeting and disclosure rules expose directors to administrative fines up to KRW 10,000,000 and possible criminal sanctions for false or non-disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return including audited financial statements, taxable income calculation, tax adjustments, and statutory corporate tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the end of the business year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year, subject to the electronic filing and extension provisions of the Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported tax penalty of 20% of the assessed corporate tax; underreported tax penalty of 10% of the omitted or understated amount, rising to 20% for intentional underreporting; statutory daily late-payment interest on unpaid corporate tax currently at approximately 0.022% per day; persistent non-payment triggers seizure of assets, tax collection orders, and eventual administrative dissolution or strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and payment accompanying the national corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority of the jurisdiction where the registered head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the end of the business year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid local corporate income tax; underreporting penalty of 10%; daily late-payment interest applies on the unpaid local corporate income tax at the statutory local tax rate; continued delinquency may trigger collection proceedings and encumbrance of the company's registered assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and audited financial statements filed by the external auditor for companies subject to mandatory external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of the Republic of Korea through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external audit must be completed before the annual general shareholders' meeting, and the audit report and audited financial statements must be filed with the FSS within fourteen (14) days after the annual general meeting; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, this entire process must align with the statutory March 31 annual meeting deadline and the corporate income tax return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the external audit report exposes the company and the auditor to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the FSS may designate another auditor and impose monetary penalties up to the statutory ceiling of KRW 20,000,000; unaudited or rejected financial statements cannot validly support the corporate tax return or the annual general meeting.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a non-listed Chusik Hoesa must appoint an independent certified public accounting firm if, as of the end of the immediately preceding business year, its total assets amount to KRW 12,000,000,000 or more, approximately USD 9,000,000; a listed company or company designated by the Financial Services Commission is also subject to mandatory external audit; Korea does not currently impose a standalone statutory turnover or headcount threshold that triggers mandatory independent audit for an ordinary unlisted company, but the Financial Services Commission may designate additional companies requiring external audit based on public interest and enforcement decree criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies required to apply IFRS, including listed and publicly accountable entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP or General Corporate Accounting Standards) for most other Chusik Hoesa; Simplified Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises for eligible small companies; all accounting is required to comply with the Commercial Act, the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, and the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing equivalent to a European registrable beneficial owner return. The Chusik Hoesa is required to keep an accurate Register of Members at its registered office; share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members before the transferee can exercise shareholder rights against the company. Tax-relevant shareholding and beneficial ownership changes must be reflected in the annual corporate income tax return, and significant foreign-investment or foreign-exchange control events must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and to the Foreign Exchange Information System within thirty (30) days of the triggering event. On-site inspection of the statutory registers must be permitted to shareholders and entitled third parties during the annual general meeting period; any transfer that changes the ultimate beneficial ownership of a Korean financial relationship must also be updated with the relevant financial institution under the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,500 per year for a registered office or outsourced corporate secretarial agent in Seoul; combined local tax and accounting coordination services are commonly quoted at USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 for a mandatory external audit performed by a licensed Korean certified public accounting firm, depending on group size, transaction complexity, and application of K-IFRS versus K-GAAP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax (progressive 10%/20%/22%/25% brackets), plus 10% local income tax surtax, yielding a 27.5% top aggregate rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad patent box; R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act of 25-50% for eligible in-house R&D and SME R&D; tax exemption or reduction for technology transfer income; preferential rates or cash grants for advanced foreign-invested high-tech business; zero-rated VAT for exported SaaS; loss carryforward of 5 years for this regime

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 4 Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement (with attached schedules, foreign transaction reports, and related-party disclosures) e-filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; semi-annual estimated corporate tax prepayments due for companies with prior-year tax liability
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year Chusik Hoesa); withholding for outbound dividends remitted by the 10th day of the month following dividend payment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter a full 12-month period consistent with articles of incorporation; for a newly incorporated non-resident-owned Chusik Hoesa, do not create a short period unless the first filing is the only short period permitted; confirm all cross-border transactions are included in this period for transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, trade name, Korean taxpayer registration number, registered address, and main business (B2B Enterprise SaaS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the legal form Chusik Hoesa, ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; list representative director and any foreign nominee shareholder; attach shareholder register showing tax residence of each non-resident owner for accurate dividend withholding and treaty eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue / total sales (subscription fees, per-seat licenses, usage charges, implementation fees, recurring payments from B2B enterprise contracts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all SaaS revenue on accrual basis under Korean GAAP or K-IFRS; allocate domestic versus export revenue separately; do not classify bundled software subscriptions as royalties unless there is a separate intellectual property license for withholding; attach export documentation for zero-rated VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and operating expenses (server hosting, R&D, salaries, marketing, intercompany fees, royalties, interest)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the arm's-length standard to every intercompany payment; verify and withhold on payments to foreign related parties for services or intangibles; maintain local-file and master-file documentation for all cross-border related-party transactions to substantiate deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income before loss carryforward (revenue minus non-deductible adjustments, transfer-pricing adjustments, thin capitalization, CFC inclusions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include upward transfer-pricing adjustments for understated foreign-related revenue; reduce by foreign tax credits; disclose any DTA positions and beneficial ownership of IP; if a foreign affiliate provides SaaS services, ensure no double deduction of costs by both entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax (national) applying progressive rates and local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate at statutory rates; add 10% local surcharge on national corporate income tax; for dividends to non-resident shareholders, remember that corporate tax is borne by the Chusik Hoesa, while distribution withholding is a separate obligation at profit repatriation stage; no imputation credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, interim prepayments, and refunds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim R&D and investment tax credits; attach form showing foreign income and related foreign tax credit if the Korean entity earned overseas SaaS income; reconcile semi-annual estimated prepayments; non-resident shareholders do not receive a credit against Korean corporate income tax for Korean dividend withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedules: related-party transactions, foreign company tax avoidance prevention (CFC), consolidated or international tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File complete international transaction disclosure; certify that medium-to-large enterprises have prepared Local File and Master File; state all beneficial owners; if a shareholder is an intermediary resident in a tax-treaty country, substantiate that it has real economic substance and carries out CIGA before claiming reduced withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and underreporting surcharge under Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-3 and 47-4: 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing, 10% for underreporting, 40% for fraudulent false returns; daily late-payment surcharge applies until full payment; criminal fraud threshold under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 3 times the evaded tax, aggravated for habitual or large evasion; directors can be jointly liable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate (20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax) on dividend distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders, absent treaty relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying an outbound dividend, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Korean payer with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its residence jurisdiction and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration. The payer files the Tax Treaty Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction Application with the competent Korean tax office; if the reduced treaty rate is not applied at source because evidence was late, the non-resident can seek a refund within 3 years of the withholding year. In typical OECD parallels, direct dividend rate is 10%, or 5% for a qualified shareholding such as 25% or more, and the payer must maintain supporting corporate registers, board minutes, and ownership records to prove no treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source withholding on interest and royalties paid to foreign related companies is 22% aggregate (20% plus 2% local surtax); ordinary DTA reduced rate is generally 10% for interest and royalties, or 0% on arm's-length interest under certain treaties; royalties for software may be characterized as business income if the transfer qualifies as a sale of rights, while ongoing SaaS fees may escape royalty withholding if paid as service income; intercompany interest must also satisfy arm's-length rate and thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 aggregate related-party cross-border transactions for full Local File and Master File; KRW 5,000,000,000 simplified documentation for each intercompany goods, service, intangible, or loan category
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but applies economic substance through the substance-over-form principle, the OECD/G20 BEPS anti-avoidance standard, and the general anti-abuse rule in the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA Article 5). A Chusik Hoesa must perform its core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea: real employees, substantive B2B SaaS contracts, marketing and technical support, server and development activity, and independent board decisions. A foreign intermediary shareholder must have genuine offices, decision-making, actual employees, and risk-bearing capacity; otherwise the NTS can disregard the intermediary, deny treaty benefits, and reattribute profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through False Annual Reporting and Electronic Tax Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting B2B SaaS subscription revenue, issuing fraudulent electronic tax invoices, creating fictitious cost entries, or using undisclosed foreign payment accounts to avoid Korean corporate income tax and VAT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9 and Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-3 and 47-4: additional tax of 20%-40% of the unpaid corporate income tax, daily late-payment penalty, and criminal fine up to three times the evaded tax; fraudulent electronic tax invoices carry separate imprisonment sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors knowingly instigate or conceal the fraud; directors become jointly and severally liable for all unpaid national taxes and penalties, may be blacklisted as habitual tax delinquents with travel and exit restrictions, and face imprisonment up to 5 years for aggravated evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Failures in the Related-Party Disclosure Regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to a foreign related party located in a low-tax jurisdiction without actual services, IP substance, or capacity; failing to prepare and submit Local File or Master File when the statutory threshold is met; charging a non-arm's-length profit margin in the Korean SaaS operating entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 5 and Corporate Tax Act Article 52 authorize adjustment to the arm's-length amount; deduction is denied for excess payments; 40% fraudulent understatement penalty and 10%-20% negligent understatement penalty apply; failure to comply with documentation imposes an independent penalty surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return or direct the intercompany pricing are personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties if they acted intentionally; Korean authorities can disregard the separate legal personality of a foreign affiliate used solely to avoid tax; senior officers face criminal liability for filing false international transaction statements and travel bans from NTS blacklisting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Shareholder, Treaty Shopping, and Beneficial-Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or using a nominee intermediary in a jurisdiction with a favorable Korean DTA, with no employees, offices, economic function, or decision-making, solely to extract Korean SaaS dividends or royalties and claim a reduced withholding rate; failure to substantiate beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization under LCITA Article 5 and the Korea-treaty beneficial-ownership requirement; the distribution is re-taxed at the 22% aggregate withholding rate plus penalty surcharges for non-withholding; false treaty exemption filing may be treated as tax evasion with fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Korean Chusik Hoesa who signed the treaty-benefit withholding application and knew the shareholder was a shell bear personal civil liability for the deficient withholding tax; criminal exposure includes imprisonment for aiding tax evasion; the representative director's passport and travel may be restricted and assets seized under National Tax Collection procedures.
